Feature flags evaluate locally via lightweight SDKs (the JavaScript SDK is 9KB) with zero network requests at runtime.

GrowthBook is available as open-source self-hosted, cloud-managed, or with a managed warehouse option.

FeatBit is an open-source feature flag and toggle management platform designed to help development teams ship faster, deploy safely, and conduct real-time experiments.
It provides the infrastructure for managing feature rollouts, A/B testing, and targeted feature delivery, allowing businesses to validate new features quickly and control their release to specific user segments.
The platform emphasizes data privacy and security through its self-hosted deployment options, ensuring data remains within the user's infrastructure.
FeatBit is ideal for development teams, product managers, and enterprises looking for a cost-effective yet powerful solution for feature management, especially those building AI agents and software.
It supports various programming languages and integrates with modern AI tools, enabling developers to incorporate feature flags seamlessly into their workflows.
With options for Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud deployments, FeatBit caters to different operational needs, from development and testing to production-grade environments.
The platform's core value proposition includes significant cost savings compared to traditional solutions, full transparency with its open-source nature, and complete control over data and infrastructure.
It offers unlimited seats, service connections, and monthly active users (MAU) in its self-hosted free and enterprise versions, providing predictable pricing without escalating costs as teams scale.
Developer Rocket Fuel for Feature Flags, Dynamic Logging, and Secret Management.
Prefab provides a comprehensive platform for managing feature flags, dynamic logging, and secrets, designed specifically for developers.
It aims to streamline development workflows by offering real-time configuration changes, robust editor integrations, and detailed observability into flag usage.
The platform helps engineering teams maintain control over their applications, enabling safe rollouts, A/B testing, and instant debugging without redeployments.
Prefab is built for engineering teams of all sizes, from startups to large enterprises, who need granular control over their application's behavior in production.
It addresses common pain points like stale feature flags, costly debug logging, and insecure secret sharing, allowing developers to stay in their flow and focus on building.
Its developer-first approach emphasizes ease of use, powerful tooling, and transparent, usage-based pricing.
View Details Try Free Prefab alternatives →
Manage feature flags, experiments, and configurations across your software delivery lifecycle.
Configure8 is a platform designed to help development teams manage feature flags, A/B tests, and dynamic configurations.
It aims to provide a centralized system for controlling feature rollouts, enabling progressive delivery, and conducting experiments without requiring code deployments.
The platform integrates with existing development workflows to give engineers and product managers granular control over who sees what features and when.
It caters to organizations looking to adopt or mature their use of feature flagging for safer deployments, personalized user experiences, and data-driven decision-making.
By decoupling feature releases from code deployments, Configure8 helps reduce deployment risk, accelerate release cycles, and facilitate continuous experimentation.
It provides tools for targeting specific user segments, scheduling flag changes, and monitoring the impact of new features.
View Details Try Free Configure8 alternatives →
Optimizely MCP
Query and create feature flags, experiments, audiences and results from an AI client.
The Optimizely Experimentation MCP server gives AI assistants direct access to a feature flagging and experimentation project, so defining a test can happen next to the code that implements it.
An agent can list projects, environments, flags, variations, rulesets and audiences, create or update a flag and its targeting rules, define experiment variations and traffic allocation, and read results including how each variation performed against a metric.
Pairing it with a coding agent is the main use case.
A developer adding a flag in the codebase can have the assistant create the matching flag and rollout rule in Optimizely, reference the right SDK key and environment, and later ask whether an experiment has reached a decision instead of switching to the results dashboard to read the numbers.
Reading audience and event definitions also helps an agent write instrumentation that matches what the experiment expects to receive.
It is meant for product engineers, growth and experimentation teams, and product managers running tests on Optimizely, especially those working inside an AI coding client where the flag and the code change belong to the same task.
Authentication uses an Optimizely API token scoped to a project, so what an agent can read or modify follows the account's existing permissions rather than a blanket key.
View Details Try Free Optimizely MCP alternatives →
Feature flags and A/B testing versioned in your git repo
dif.sh is a developer tool that brings feature flags and A/B testing directly into your code repository.
Instead of relying on a separate service, each flag or experiment is a single markdown file with structured frontmatter, versioned in git and reviewable in pull requests.
The CLI and SDK are free and open-source, allowing you to define experiments, run builds that detect conflicts, and generate a context file that coding agents can read on startup.
An optional cloud layer provides live metrics, team dashboards, and PR write-back, billed per event with unlimited seats.
View Details Try Free dif.sh alternatives →
Open-source feature flag infrastructure
Flipt is open-source feature flagging that you can self-host completely. Feature toggles, experiments, and configuration-flag management without SaaS costs. The deployment is simple. The feature set covers common needs. Full control remains with you. Teams wanting feature flags without SaaS dependencies choose Flipt for self-hosted flag management.
Streamline, test, and automate application configurations across all environments.
Configu is an end-to-end application configuration management platform that reimagines how organizations handle environment variables, secrets, feature flags, and other code-related configurations.
It acts as a single source of truth, preventing misconfigurations by validating each configuration value, removing duplicates, and checking for dependencies before they can cause issues.
This ensures that only correct and compliant configurations are deployed.
The platform automates the propagation of configuration changes across various environments, from development to production, and integrates seamlessly with existing toolchains including CI/CD pipelines, runtimes, PaaS, clouds, databases, secret managers, and feature flags.
By adopting a Configuration-as-Code approach, Configu enables developers and DevOps teams to collaborate effectively, manage configuration schemas alongside code, and maintain version history for easy rollbacks and auditing.
It's designed for developers and DevOps professionals seeking to enhance security, compliance, and efficiency in their configuration management processes.
View Details Try Free Configu alternatives →
GoFeatureFlag
Ship faster, reduce risk, and build at scale with simple, open-source feature flagging.
GO Feature Flag is an open-source feature flagging solution designed to help development teams modify system behavior without changing code.
It enables organizations to decouple deployment from release, allowing for progressive feature rollouts, A/B testing, and targeted user experiences.
The tool focuses on simplicity, offering a lightweight setup and integration with existing development workflows.
This solution is ideal for developers, product managers, and businesses looking to accelerate innovation, reduce deployment risks, and gain insights into feature usage.
By providing advanced rollout capabilities and supporting various data storage and notification systems, GO Feature Flag empowers teams to test in production, empower stakeholders, and continuously improve their software delivery process.
It embraces open standards through OpenFeature, ensuring vendor neutrality and broad language support.
LaunchDarkly MCP
Manage feature flags from your editor, terminal, or chat
LaunchDarkly MCP is the Model Context Protocol interface to LaunchDarkly, the feature management platform used to ship code behind flags, control rollouts and disable a bad release without a redeploy.
The server wraps the LaunchDarkly REST API so an assistant in an editor, terminal or chat client can read and change flag state with a service token, instead of a developer switching to the LaunchDarkly dashboard mid-task.
Typical exposure covers the account hierarchy of projects and environments plus the flags inside it: list flags, read a flag configuration and its targeting rules per environment, create a flag, toggle it on or off, adjust rollout percentages, and manage the segments used for targeting.
Servers also surface supporting objects such as metrics and experiments, and the AI configuration entities LaunchDarkly uses to version model settings and prompts behind the same flag machinery.
The point is closing the loop between writing code and controlling it.
An agent that just added a flag guard in a pull request can register the flag, wire the default rule and hand back the key in one pass.
Teams also use it for release chores: check which flags are stale, confirm what is enabled in production before a deploy, or flip a kill switch during an incident.
Because writes are real production changes, scope the token to the projects and environments the agent should touch and keep destructive actions behind an explicit confirmation.

Why choose free feature flags software?
Free feature flags tools are an excellent way to get started without financial commitment. Whether you're a startup, freelancer, or small business, these tools offer essential features at no cost.
What to look for in free feature flags tools
Feature limitations : Understand what's included in the free tier vs paid plans
Usage limits : Check for restrictions on users, storage, or API calls
Data ownership : Ensure you own your data and can export it
Support : Free tiers often have community-only support
Upgrade path : Consider future needs if you outgrow the free tier
Free vs Freemium: what's the difference?
Free 100% free, no payment ever
Completely free with no paid upgrades available. Best for simple, focused workflows that don't require advanced features.
Freemium Free tier + paid upgrades
Generous free tier with optional paid plans that unlock advanced features, higher limits, or team collaboration.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the best free feature flags tool in 2026?
PostHog is our free feature flags pick in 2026. On the full category ranking, LaunchDarkly is our overall feature flags pick. PostHog offers a free plan alongside paid plans: Open-source product analytics with event tracking, feature flags, and session recording.
Is PostHog really free forever?
PostHog uses a freemium model: there is a permanent free tier you can use without a credit card, plus optional paid plans that unlock higher usage limits and advanced features. The free tier itself does not expire.
What does the free tier of feature flags software typically include?
Free feature flags tools typically include the core workflow features needed to evaluate the product. Paid plans usually unlock higher usage limits, team collaboration, advanced analytics, integrations, and priority support. The specific cap differs per tool.
When should I upgrade from a free feature flags tool?
Upgrade when you hit one of the free tier ceilings: usage quota (output count, storage, contacts, projects), team size, or a paid-only feature your workflow depends on.
Are there feature flags tools that are 100% free, not just freemium?
Yes. We found 1 completely free feature flags tool (no paid upgrade path) and 14 tools with a permanent free tier alongside paid plans. Flipt is 100% free.
Is free feature flags software good enough for business use?
Yes, for most startups, freelancers, and small teams. PostHog and Statsig both offer free tiers robust enough for production workflows. Larger teams typically upgrade when they need SSO, audit logs, advanced permissions, or usage past the free quota.
